q: Why is ROAS increasing while net profit is declining?

checks.what: tool: ROAS attempted or derived from its definition

answer:
Short answer: the data disagree with the premise — ROAS rose while the company’s net loss actually narrowed. Net ROAS increased from 0.724 → 0.936 (+28.9%), and net profit moved from a loss of ₹-5,15,592 → ₹-67,866 (loss narrowed).

What’s behind it
- Big cut in ad spend (largest driver). Ad spend (P&L basis) fell ₹18,89,707 → ₹10,87,884 (−42.4%). Because spend fell proportionally more than contribution margin, ROAS (contribution per rupee of ad) improved even though sales fell.
- Contribution margin fell too, and reduced profitability relative to sales. Contribution margin dropped ₹13,74,115 → ₹10,20,018 (−25.8%), which reduced net profit but by less than the ad‑spend saving, so the overall loss shrank.
- Volume and acquisition fell. Orders and new customers declined (orders down ~33%, new customers down ~36%), so sales fell (net sales down ~30%) — that’s why contribution margin fell.
- Net result: ROAS rises because ad spend per order fell faster than contribution margin per order improved; net profit did not decline — it improved (loss narrowed) because the ad spend cuts outweighed the drop in margin.

Worth checking: whether the ad‑spend reduction was intentional (campaign cuts or paused budgets) and whether the sales drop is acceptably temporary — if spend is restored, ROAS may fall and profit could change.

Period: 2026-09-17..2026-10-16 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-16
